ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the Cartesian coordinate system xOy, the graph of the linear function $y=-x+6$, denoted as ${l}_{1}$, intersects the $x$ and $y$ axes at points A and B, respectively. The graph of the direct variation function, denoted as ${l}_{2}$, intersects ${l}_{1}$ at point C ($m$, 5). What is the area of $\triangle AOC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} The solution for the linear function $y=-x+6$ and its intersection point A with the x-axis is found by setting $y=0$, and solving $-x+6=0$ to get $x=6$,\\
$\therefore$OA=6,\\
The area of $\triangle AOC$ is $S_{\triangle AOC}=\frac{1}{2}OA\cdot y_c=\frac{1}{2}\times 6\times 5=\boxed{15}$.

Because C lies on segment AB as shown, triangle AOC is the part of triangle AOB left after removing triangle BOC, so its area is 18-3=15.
